title: Understanding the Model
text: To find the bias and variance, start by considering the model function $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(z\right)=\theta z$$. Since $$x=1$$, think about how you would choose theta to best fit the data point.

title: Optimal Theta
text: With no noise (sigma**2=0), the observed $$y$$ is exactly g(x). What does this imply about the relationship between theta and A when $$x=1$$?

title: Choosing Theta
text: If $$x=1$$ and $$y=g(x)$$, what should theta be to make $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x\right)=y$$?

title: Bias Calculation
text: The bias of a model is the difference between the expected prediction of the model and the true function value at a test point. What happens to this difference when theta is chosen optimally?

title: Bias Value
text: Given that theta is chosen such that $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(z\right)=g(z)$$ at $$z=1$$, what is the bias?

title: Variance Insight
text: Variance measures how much the model's predictions vary for different training sets. With only one data point and no noise, how much variation do you expect?

title: Variance Value
text: Considering there is no noise and only one data point, what is the variance of the model's prediction at $$z=1$$?
